setup_data_boundary: If you already have a permitted Windows copy, select cybermage.exe with its containing folder as the working directory. Choose Play explicitly. The player runs the original x86 code through an interpreter with native services; this does not prevent useful existing-copy registration.

The game accepts your own CyberMage DOS v1.01F ISO 9660 .iso or CM_HI.EXE from its CYBERMAG folder. BIN/CUE and other executable versions are outside this input contract. Its first-Play picker verifies and copies required files to iso/CYBERMAG beside the player without changing the original. It does not import original DOS saves/settings or require optional SC-55 firmware.

The upstream player owns runtime replacement and setup. Keep iso/CYBERMAG, run and NATIVE.CNF backed up with the application closed; a custom --root uses that chosen data root instead. Existing imported destinations are not overwritten automatically; retain a working folder before following upstream repair instructions. Portcove registration leaves all files external and provides no managed update, backup or rollback.

setup_data_boundary: This is BTFighter’s Godot fork of JHDev2006 Super Mario World Remastered, not a native 65816 recompilation. Use an existing copy you are permitted to use and select its exported game executable, with that game folder as the working directory. Keep its companion data files together. Current releases are RAR archives; Portcove does not extract RAR. Older ZIP releases do not resolve the separate bundled-artwork question.

Place your own baserom.sfc in the SuperMarioWorldRemastered user-data folder shown by the game’s ROM screen. Its checker accepts specific USA, Japanese and European SNES hashes, including some headered variants; an additional accepted hash has no independently established edition here. This gate checks the ROM but does not extract or establish permission for the already bundled sprites/music. Use upstream’s exact recognized edition; no Core original-file receipt is claimed.

Both this fork and its archived parent configure the same SuperMarioWorldRemastered user-data directory. Back up that actual Godot profile with both games closed before switching, and keep each working runtime; save compatibility between forks is unqualified. The game normally uses %APPDATA%/SuperMarioWorldRemastered on Windows and $XDG_DATA_HOME/SuperMarioWorldRemastered or ~/.local/share/SuperMarioWorldRemastered on Linux. Updates and backups remain yours; registration neither migrates the parent nor provides managed rollback.

setup_data_boundary: Select EarthBound Companion.exe with its own folder as the working directory, then choose Play explicitly. Use its guided setup with your own clean USA EarthBound ROM. The launcher builds native game data and optional supported Redux content; Portcove does not run its helpers during discovery. This is a distinct implementation from nickclyde/EarthBoundRecomp and does not change that integration or retained contracts. If your existing launcher uses a custom data root, retain its --data-root argument and chosen directory when registering: enter --data-root and the directory as two separate argument lines. Otherwise it opens the default profile instead.

The ordinary Windows build uses the launcher folder as its data root; portable/preview builds can use %LOCALAPPDATA%/EarthBoundCompanionPreview instead. Keep the complete actual Companion data root, including Game, Profiles, UserData, msu, settings, supported mods and generated content, backed up with the game closed. Original, Redux and generated seeds have separate save namespaces. Make a normal in-game phone save before changing versions: quick states are build-specific, and runtime rollback does not restore earlier saves or guarantee older compatibility. Use the launcher’s own supported backup/restore and migration controls; retain original ROMs and working runtimes separately.

The launcher and its helpers own preparation, version-specific content generation and replacement. Registration leaves every external file untouched and does not promise Portcove-managed update, backup, restore or rollback. Fresh foundation redistribution/GPL qualification remains unresolved; a conditional existing-copy guide is not binary-distribution clearance.

setup_data_boundary: On first Play, select your own Stunts 1.1 folder or ZIP in the game’s welcome screen. Other 4D Sports Driving revisions are outside this input claim. Setup requires Internet access to fetch its translation map; it normally caches that map by app version and imports the original into its profile. Retain your original files for reimport if storage fails. No original game files are supplied.

Saves, tracks, replays, high scores, preferences, imported originals and cached maps live outside the runtime: %APPDATA%/Stunts HD on Windows, or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Stunts HD (normally ~/.config/Stunts HD) on Linux. Back up that whole profile with the app closed. Portcove manages the downloaded runtime only; its backup does not include this profile or chosen screenshot/export destinations. F6 exports are not a complete restorable profile backup.

For an existing Windows copy select Stunts HD.exe; on Linux select stunts-hd with its containing folder. The upstream browser player at https://stunts-recomp.pages.dev/ has separate browser-site storage. macOS uses the upstream application through the OS; ARM and AppImage routes remain upstream-owned. A missing version cache downloads a mutable upstream map, so first setup after a version change or runtime rollback may need Internet and may fail if that map no longer matches. Preserve existing cached maps; offline/historical-map and save compatibility are not guaranteed.

setup_data_boundary: For an existing copy you are permitted to use, select abuse.exe on Windows or abuse on Linux with its game folder as the working directory. Keep its compatible data and libraries together; ABUSE_PATH overrides the asset root. The current release offers Windows and macOS packages; Linux here describes an already prepared native copy, not an offered Linux archive or a Portcove build. macOS uses the upstream application through the OS, not a private bundle binary.

The reviewed SDL code normally uses SDL_GetPrefPath("abuse", "data") for saves/settings: %APPDATA%/abuse/data on Windows, or $XDG_DATA_HOME/abuse/data (normally ~/.local/share/abuse/data) on Linux. ABUSE_SAVE_PATH overrides it; if preference-path creation fails upstream falls back to the current working directory. Preserve that actual location, custom levels/mods and the working data folder with the game closed. The local_save flag alone is not proof that saves are beside the executable.

Registration leaves the external files untouched. You and upstream own updates and backups; Portcove supplies no managed backup or rollback. Upstream mentions a public-domain data subset, but its exact clean subset and compatibility with this release still need acceptance. Do not automatically replace mixed bundled assets or claim that a root code license covers music and soundfonts.
